newsitem.title: USA: Canada spot natgas prices rise on storage refills.
newsitem.headline: Canada spot natgas prices rise on storage refills.

text.p: Canadian spot natural gas prices were mostly higher Monday as storage injections continued at a brisk pace in the West and an unexpected outage spurred additional demand across the border.
At the AECO storage hub, prices rose gradually throughout today's session to about C$1.54-1.59 per gigajoule (GJ) as buyers replenished storage inventories.
May AECO prices were talked at C$1.58-1.60 per GJ, traders said.
At Sumas, Wash., prices edged into the low-$1.20s per million British thermal units (mmBtu).

An unscheduled outage at Pacific Gas and Electric's 1,073 megawatt (MW) Diablo Canyon 2 nuclear unit Saturday attracted more northern California buyers to the export market, thereby pushing prices higher, market sources said.
The company said the unit would likely restart in a couple of days.
At Niagara, prices were up at least five cents to the low-$2.20s per mmBtu as colder weather in the East triggered a resurgence in buying interest.
